version_verification_method: catboost --version emits git commit info, not a semver string. Commit shown (b1bd2a6d77219e82a1acfcedfccb8e6f6c1ee084) and branch (tags/v1.2.10) match the pinned upstream SHA in the ticket brief.
fit_command: catboost fit --learn-set smoke_data.csv --column-description smoke.cd --delimiter , --has-header --loss-function Logloss -i 20 --depth 4 --learning-rate 0.1 --random-seed 42 -T 1 --model-file smoke_model.cbm --logging-level Silent
calc_command: catboost calc --input-path smoke_data.csv --column-description smoke.cd --delimiter , --has-header -m smoke_model.cbm --output-path smoke_predictions.tsv --prediction-type RawFormulaVal,Probability

determinism.method: fit+calc run twice from scratch in separate clean directories, thread-count pinned to 1 (-T 1) to eliminate cross-thread histogram-order nondeterminism
determinism.model_file_note: smoke_model.cbm SHA256 differed between the two runs despite identical predictions; CatBoost embeds a training timestamp/GUID in model metadata. Not investigated further (out of scope for this ticket); does not affect oracle validity since predictions are what the differential harness compares.

cli_precision_note: catboost calc's default TSV output prints doubles at ~10 significant digits, not a full float64 round-trip repr (17 sig digits). No --precision flag exists on calc (confirmed via `calc -?`). smoke_predictions.json preserves every digit the CLI emitted (float() parse + JSON dump, no truncation added), but the CLI itself is the precision ceiling — flag this if the harness ever needs bit-exact float64 comparison against the Python oracle.

run_worker.help_text: run a worker (for the distributed mode)
args: {-T|--thread-count} VAL worker thread count (default: core count)
--node-port VAL         TCP port for this worker; default is 0
run_worker.note: All run-worker flags are optional per --help (no required positional args). Distributed-mode wiring (master/worker handshake) not exercised in this ticket — out of scope (brief explicitly excludes distributed-training work).
